title: Singleton: two calls, one reference
intro: The static reference retains the object. CREATE PRIVATE alone is not enough.
context: Local class definitions and implementations in a teaching report or class pool.
code:
CLASS lcl_settings DEFINITION FINAL CREATE PRIVATE.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS get_instance
      RETURNING VALUE(instance) TYPE REF TO lcl_settings.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    CLASS-DATA shared_instance TYPE REF TO lcl_settings.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_settings IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_instance.
    IF shared_instance IS NOT BOUND.
      shared_instance = NEW #( ).
    ENDIF.
    instance = shared_instance.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

" Inside the caller's executable method:
" DATA(first) = lcl_settings=>get_instance( ).
" DATA(second) = lcl_settings=>get_instance( ).
" ASSERT first = second.

highlights.label: Control creation
highlights.explanation: Callers cannot use NEW directly. They request the object through get_instance. The class retains one reference in CLASS-DATA.

highlights.label: Create once, reuse later
highlights.explanation: The first call creates the object. Later calls skip NEW and return the already bound reference.

highlights.label: Check the lifetime
highlights.explanation: Put these statements in an executable method and remove the comment markers. Both references are equal within this internal session. Another session has its own static data.

outcome: The caller gets the same instance twice in one internal session.
caveat: This demonstrates instance lifetime, not a configuration loader. No shared memory, locking or automatic cache invalidation is implemented. Do not keep order-specific mutable state here.

title: Facade: one preview operation, three collaborators
intro: The UI asks for a delivery preview. The facade coordinates the details.
context: Method body of your application facade. The three collaborators are injected interfaces with the methods shown below.
code:
METHOD preview_delivery.
  DATA(ls_order) = order_reader->read( order_id ).
  DATA(lt_packages) = packer->pack( ls_order ).
  result = carrier->estimate( lt_packages ).
ENDMETHOD.

" The UI only needs this operation:
" DATA(ls_preview) = delivery_facade->preview_delivery( order_id ).

highlights.label: Coordinate the steps
highlights.explanation: Read the order, calculate packages, then estimate delivery. If a collaborator raises a declared exception, the method does not continue to the next step.

highlights.label: Keep the caller simple
highlights.explanation: The caller knows preview_delivery instead of repeating all three steps. The facade still exposes its result and failures clearly.

outcome: Several callers can reuse one clearly named business operation.
caveat: Teaching fragment: define the facade signature, result type, interfaces, constructor injection and declared exceptions in your application. These are fictional collaborators, not released SAP APIs. This read-only preview does not create a LUW or issue COMMIT.

title: A table action with a shared changeset
intro: Request atomic grouping for selected instances in a supporting Fiori elements client.
context: Metadata extension of your own projection ZC_Order, which allows metadata extensions and exposes the Approve action through its service.

highlights.label: Expose the action
highlights.explanation: Use the actual exposed RAP action name. The label is presentation text; it does not create the action implementation.

highlights.label: Choose the group
highlights.explanation: #CHANGE_SET requests one changeset for the selected instances. #ISOLATED is the default and allows independent changesets. Either may be carried in $batch.

highlights.label: Verify the failure case
highlights.explanation: Select three orders, make one invalid, inspect metadata and the network payload, then verify that none of the grouped updates persisted. Do not infer grouping from the URL alone.

outcome: In the supported all-or-nothing scenario, one rejected order prevents the whole shared changeset from committing.
caveat: Requires a matching projection, behavior, service and supported Fiori elements/OData version. The annotation does not configure arbitrary freestyle clients or provide rollback for already committed remote effects.
